title: Unit 3: Cultural Values - Tenses Overview 🌍
content: 📌 Welcome Freshmen Students to Communicative English Skills I (EnLa101)! 👋✨ PART 1: CORE CONCEPTS & DEFINITIONS In this lesson, we examine, contrast, and master four fundamental verb tenses in English grammar for Unit 3. ========================================= 1. Simple Present Tense (መደበኛ አሁን ጊዜ) 🔄 ========================================= • Definition: Expresses routines, daily habits, general facts, universal truths, laws of nature, and permanent situations. • Examples: The sun rises in the east. Ronaldo comes from Portugal. 👉ሁልጊዜ የሚደረጉ ድርጊቶች፣ ልማዶች፣ ቋሚ ሁኔታዎች እና አጠቃላይ እውነታዎችን ለመግለፅ ያገለግላል። ========================================= 2. Simple Past Tense (ኃላፊ ጊዜ) 📅 ========================================= • Definition: Expresses completed actions that occurred at a specific, finished time in the past. • Examples: I visited Gondar last year. She finished her assignment yesterday. 👉ባለፈ ጊዜ ውስጥ በተወሰነ ሰዓት/ጊዜ (Specific Time) ተከስቶ ሙሉ በሙሉ የተጠናቀቀ ድርጊት።

title: Unit 3: Present Perfect & Past Perfect Tenses ⏱️
content: 📌 3. Present Perfect Tense (የቅርብ ኃላፊ / አሁን አገናኝ ጊዜ) 🔗 • Definition: Connects the past with the present; used for actions happening at an unspecified time, past actions with a visible present result, life experiences, or ongoing situations that started in the past. • Examples: We have lived in this city for ten years. She has lost her keys (she cannot open the door now). 👉ባለፈ ጊዜ የተከሰተ ነገር ግን አሁን ላይ ውጤቱ የሚታይ፣ ወይም የህይወት ልምድ፣ ወይም ሳይጠናቀቅ እስከ አሁን የቀጠለ ድርጊት። ========================================= 4. Past Perfect Tense (የኃላፊ ኃላፊ ጊዜ) ⏳ ========================================= • Definition: Emphasizes that one past action occurred prior to another past action in the past (the earlier past action). • Examples: After the students had finished the test, they left the hall. 👉ባለፈ ጊዜ ውስጥ ከሌላ ድርጊት በፊት ቀድሞ የተፈጸመ ድርጊትን ያሳያል።

title: Unit 3: Formulas & Key Signal Words 📊
content: 📌 Comprehensive Structural Formulas & Key Signal Words: 1. Simple Present Tense 🔄 • Formula: Subject + Verb (V1 / V-s / V-es) + Object • Signal Words: always, usually, every day, often, generally, normally, facts • Example: He works in a central bank. 2. Simple Past Tense 📅 • Formula: Subject + Verb (V2 - Past Form) + Object • Signal Words: yesterday, last (week/month/year), ago, in (past year, e.g. 2010), just now • Example: I went to Adama last week. 3. Present Perfect Tense 🔗 • Formula: Subject + have / has + Verb (V3 - Past Participle) • Signal Words: since, for, ever, never, already, yet, recently, so far, up to now • Example: We have lived here for 25 years. 4. Past Perfect Tense ⏳ • Formula: Subject + had + Verb (V3 - Past Participle) • Signal Words: before, after, by the time, as soon as, until • Example: I had seen the film before reading the novel.

title: Unit 3: Exam Rules & Tense Combination Pitfalls 🚨
content: 📌 Key Combination Rules & Exam Pitfalls to Avoid: • Rule 1: Past Perfect + Simple Past Combination ⏳➕📅 When two completed actions happened in the past, the earlier event uses Past Perfect (had + V3), and the subsequent event uses Simple Past (V2). - Formula A: Past Perfect (had + V3) + before + Simple Past (V2) - Formula B: After + Past Perfect (had + V3), Simple Past (V2) - Formula C: By the time + Simple Past (V2), Past Perfect (had + V3) - Example: After Larry had seen the film on TV, he decided to buy the book. • Rule 2: Specific Finished Time vs. Unspecified Present Result 🎯 Use Simple Past when a specific finished time is stated (yesterday, in 2015). Use Present Perfect when time is unmentioned or when the result is visible in the present. - Example A: I bought a new phone yesterday. (Finished past time) - Example B: Janet has gone home. (Present result: She is not here now) • Rule 3: Since vs. For Distinction 📍 - Since: Marks a specific starting time point (since 2008, since morning). - For: Measures a duration or period of time (for 5 years, for two hours).

title: Unit 3: Stative Verbs & Continuous Distinction 💡
content: 📌 Special Exam Rules for Perfect Tenses: • Rule 4: Stative Verbs in Perfect Tenses 🧠 Stative verbs representing knowledge, mental states, emotions, or possession (e.g., know, believe, belong, have, understand) take the simple Present Perfect rather than Present Perfect Continuous forms when expressing ongoing states up to now. ❌ Incorrect: We are knowing each other for five years. ✅ Correct: We have known each other for five years. • Rule 5: Interrupting Past Actions ⚡ When an action was in progress in the past (Past Continuous) and another action interrupted it, the interrupting action is written in the Simple Past Tense (V2). - Formula: Past Continuous + when + Simple Past (V2) - Example: The boys were playing games when it started raining.

title: Unit 3: Activity 3.2.2 Module Answers (Part 1) ✍️
content: 📌 Activity 3.2.2 Exercise Solutions with Detailed Explanations: PART A: MATCHING TENSES WITH USES (Q1) 🧩 • 1. Present Simple ➔ c, f, i - c: Expresses an action that happens again and again (Routine / Habit). - f: Expresses a fact that is true for a long time (Permanent situation). - i: Expresses a fact that is always true (Universal truth). • 2. Past Simple ➔ d, h - d: Expresses a finished action in the past. - h: Expresses a past situation or habit. • 3. Present Perfect ➔ a, e, g - a: Expresses an experience in one's life. - e: Expresses an action that began in the past and still continues. - g: Expresses a past action that has a visible present result. • 4. Past Perfect ➔ b - b: Makes clear that one action in the past happened before another action in the past.

title: Unit 3: Activity 3.2.2 Module Answers (Part 2) ✍️
content: 📌 PART B: IDENTIFICATION OF TENSE USES (Q2) 🔍 • a. I go to work by car. ➔ Habit / Routine action (Present Simple) Explanation: Describes a regular daily routine. • b. Ronaldo comes from Portugal. ➔ Fact true for a long time (Present Simple) Explanation: States an enduring origin fact. • c. He works in a bank. ➔ Permanent situation (Present Simple) Explanation: Describes an ongoing long-term job or state. • d. I went to Adama last week. ➔ Finished action in the past (Past Simple) Explanation: Completed past action with specific time expression ('last week'). • e. When I was a child, we lived... I walked... ➔ Past situation / habit (Past Simple) Explanation: Describes repeated childhood states and habits. • f. I did not go to the cinema because I had seen the film before. ➔ Action before another past action (Past Perfect) Explanation: Seeing the film (had seen) happened prior to not going to the cinema.

title: Unit 3: Activity 3.2.2 Module Answers (Part 3) ✍️
content: 📌 • g. We have lived in the same house for 25 years. ➔ Action continuing to present (Present Perfect) Explanation: Started 25 years ago and continues into the present moment. • h. Have you ever had an operation? ➔ Life experience (Present Perfect) Explanation: Inquires about an experience within one's lifetime up to now. • i. What have you done to your lip? (It's bleeding) ➔ Present result (Present Perfect) Explanation: The past event has a direct visible outcome right now (bleeding). ========================================= PART C: SENTENCE COMPLETION (Q3) 📝 ========================================= • a. I work for a company that makes printers. Explanation: Simple Present (makes) expresses a permanent fact about the company's production. • b. This photo of her was taken on holiday last year. Explanation: Simple Past Passive (was taken) is required due to 'last year'. • c. I have not seen her since 2008. Explanation: Present Perfect negative (have not seen) is mandated by 'since 2008'.

title: Unit 3: Activity 3.2.2 Module Answers (Part 4) ✍️
content: 📌 • d. I read the newspaper every morning. Explanation: Simple Present (read) denotes a daily habit signaled by 'every morning'. • e. When I visited her, she had been bed-ridden for six months. Explanation: Past Perfect (had been) shows that her illness began prior to my past visit. • f. Janet has gone home. Explanation: Present Perfect (has gone) indicates she left in the past and is currently at home. • g. She has won many awards for her contribution to classical music. Explanation: Present Perfect (has won) highlights life achievements up to the present. • h. The boys were playing games when it started raining. Explanation: Simple Past (started) expresses an interrupting short action. • i. How long have you been a social activist? Explanation: Present Perfect is used with 'How long' to ask about ongoing duration. • j. We have known each other for a long time. Explanation: Present Perfect with stative verb 'know' and duration marker 'for a long time'. • k. Since 2011 they have visited their son every year. Explanation: Present Perfect for repeated action continuing since 'Since 2011'. • l. After Larry had seen the film on TV, he decided to buy the book. Explanation: Past Perfect (had seen) represents the earlier past action after 'After'. --- ❤️ Dear EthioFresh Students!
